newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 13.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 13.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, Brand-name Products and People News.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - Publicis confirms that Michele Bleustein-Blanchet, the youngest daughter of the founder of Publicis, the late Marcel Bleustein-Blanchet, plans to sell her stake in the advertising group. But company chairman Maurice Levy denies there's been any family row over this. (Reuter)

PARIS - The advertising arm of French railways company SNCF is preparing a special network of billboards for the World Cup next year. It plans a specific offering to advertisers based on its national and regional presence. (Le Figaro)

PARIS - Credit Lyonnais' new campaign, devised by Devarieux-Villaret for newspaper adverts, explains the bank's products and aims to respond to existing clients' needs while trying to attract new clients. (Le Figaro)
MEDIA:

PARIS - A new war of words breaks out between the arch rivals of French television, Canal Plus and Television par Satellite, over pre-purchasing films made by French producers for showing on their channels. (Reuter)
PARIS - French digital satellite television station Television par Satellite (TPS) clinches its first film pre-purchase deals, TPS managing director Cyrille du Peloux says. (Reuter)
CANNES - No clear favourite for the Golden Palm award emerges halfway into the Cannes film festival in a competition diet heavy on dark, violent tales. (Reuter)

PARIS - Shares in French film company Gaumont rise strongly, setting a new 1997 high, propelled by strong figures for people going to see its latest offering, Luc Besson's "The Fifth Element", sector specialists say. (Reuter)
PARIS - Daily newspaper France Soir carries three pages on election campaign television spots devised by French political parties and describes the spots as "monotonous" and "sad". (France Soir)

PARIS - Advertising space specialist Carat sticks to its guns, saying television audiences slid sharply in France early this year, despite audience measurement body Mediametrie's denial of a slump last week. (Liberation)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
PARIS - Domestic appliance manufacturer Moulinex posts a small decline in turnover for the year to March 31, 1997, down 0.5 percent at 7.75 million francs on a like-for-like basis. (Reuter)

PARIS - French drinks and luxury goods company LVMH is expected to get around seven percent of GMG Brands, the company to be formed from a planned merger of British hotels group Grand Metropolitan Plc and British drinks firm Guinness Plc, a source close to the deal says. (Reuter)
BRUSSELS - Workers at the Renault plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium, are scheduled to hold 24-hour strike on Tuesday in protest against plans to close the site, union leaders say. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
PARIS - Nathalie Regnault is appointed director of external and internal communication at CLM/BBDO and La Compagnie BBDO. (Le Figaro)
PARIS - Albert Mathieu is appointed director in charge of external relations at Canal Plus. Up to now he was director, television films, for the group. (Le Figaro)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
For further information and news, see Reuters Advertising & Media Briefing. And visit us on the Internet at http://www.Bizinfo.reuters.com
